question: Why does cognition later apprehend an object with specific external form?
premises: Cognition can apprehend an object with specific external form.
This apprehension differs from undifferentiated apprehension.
A reason for this differentiated apprehension is indicated.
inference: The object comes to be apprehended in cognition with specific external form.
uncertainties: The causal clause is completed by the following verse.
plain_english: Because it ascends into cognition with the distinction of an external form—
